cues.zh: 欢迎！在这一集里，我要讲讲老式图形是怎么工作的。
cues.en: Welcome! In this episode I'm gonna explain how old-school graphics worked.

cues.zh: 我们先快速聊点基础数学。
cues.en: Let's talk about some basic math real quick.

cues.zh: 回到1980年代初，典型的家用电脑只有16K内存，
cues.en: Back in the early 1980s, your typical home computer had 16K of RAM,

cues.zh: 有些是32K，
cues.en: some had 32K,

cues.zh: 如果你真的钱多得没处花，可能会有64K。
cues.en: and if you really had money to burn, then you might have 64K.

cues.zh: 现在，我们来说说屏幕内存。
cues.en: Now, let's talk about screen memory.

cues.zh: 当时的视频芯片没有自己独立的内存，所以只能和CPU共用。
cues.en: The video chip back then didn't have its own bank of memory, so it had to share with the CPU.

cues.zh: 那时候典型的屏幕分辨率是320 x 200像素。
cues.en: Back then a typical screen resolution was 320 x 200 pixels.

cues.zh: 算一下你就会发现，屏幕上有64,000个像素。
cues.en: And if you do the math, you'll see there are 64,000 pixels on the screen.

cues.zh: 接下来，我们说说颜色。
cues.en: Now, let's talk about color.

cues.zh: 如果你只想要1位色，也就是基本上黑白，
cues.en: If you just wanted 1-bit color, which is essentially black and white,

cues.zh: 那么光保存屏幕信息就需要8千字节内存。
cues.en: then you would need 8 kilobytes of memory just to hold the screen information.

cues.zh: 好，这已经占掉了这些电脑相当大一块内存。
cues.en: Okay, so that takes a decent chunk of memory from all of these computers.

cues.zh: 但剩下的空间还够放你的游戏代码。
cues.en: But, it still leaves enough left over for your game code.

cues.zh: 现在，如果提高到16色，突然就需要32K，
cues.en: Now, if you bump that up to 16 colors, suddenly you need 32K,

cues.zh: 这比很多电脑的内存还多。
cues.en: which is more than many computers even had.

cues.zh: 等到了256色，你已经吃光了所有RAM，即使是高端电脑也一样，
cues.en: By the time you get to 256 colors, you've eaten up all of the RAM, even in high-end computers,

cues.zh: 所以现在没地方留给任何代码了。
cues.en: so now there's no room left for any code.

cues.zh: 而做现代风格的24位“真彩色”更是不可能。
cues.en: And doing a modern-style 24-bit "true color" would be impossible.

cues.zh: 所以工程师们相当聪明，他们想出了办法，在不占用那么多RAM的情况下，从这些老机器里榨出更多颜色，
cues.en: So the engineers were pretty smart and they figured out ways to get more color out of these old machines without using up so much RAM,

cues.zh: 基本上用了三种不同的方法，我来逐一介绍。
cues.en: and there were essentially three different methods used for this and I'm going to cover them.

cues.zh: 色元（Color cells），被
cues.en: Color cells, which were used

cues.zh: Commodore和Nintendo等许多系统采用；
cues.en: by many systems such as Commodore and Nintendo;

cues.zh: 伪彩色（artifact coloring），
cues.en: artifact coloring,

cues.zh: 主要用于Apple II和Tandy Color Computer；
cues.en: used primarily on the Apple II and the Tandy Color Computer;

cues.zh: CPU驱动的图形，比如Atari 2600和Sinclair ZX81上的。
cues.en: CPU driven graphics, such as on the Atari 2600 and the Sinclair ZX81.

cues.zh: 好，我们要介绍的第一类系统可以说是最流行的。
cues.en: Ok, so the first type of system we're going to cover was arguably the most popular.

cues.zh: 他们的做法基本上就是把屏幕缩小成更小的区块，
cues.en: Now what they did was they basically took the screen and shrunk it down into smaller sections

cues.zh: 这些区块叫做单元格或彩色单元格。
cues.en: and these sections were called cells or color cells.

cues.zh: 这样你就能改变每个特定单元格的颜色。
cues.en: That way you could change the color of each specific cell.

cues.zh: 我来演示一下这是怎么运作的。
cues.en: Let me illustrate how this works.

cues.zh: 假设这是一块黑色屏幕，
cues.en: Let's pretend this is a black screen,

cues.zh: 我们把像素放大来看。
cues.en: and let's zoom into the pixels.

cues.zh: 我这样画是为了让你看到像素之间假想的界线。
cues.en: Now I've drawn this so that you can see imaginary lines where the pixels would be.

cues.zh: 现在，我们在屏幕上放一些示例文字。
cues.en: Now, let's put some example text on the screen.

cues.zh: 此时屏幕本质上是一块1位屏幕，所以像素要么亮要么灭。
cues.en: At this point the screen is essentially a 1-bit screen so pixels are either on or they're off.

cues.zh: 那么，我们怎么给它加上颜色呢？
cues.en: So, how can we add color to this?

cues.zh: 把屏幕划分成宽8像素、高8像素的区域。
cues.en: Well, divide up the screen into areas that are 8 pixels wide and 8 pixels tall.

cues.zh: 现在，我们要划出这些区域，让你可以定义前景色和背景色。
cues.en: Now, we'll make these areas where you can define a foreground and a background color.

cues.zh: 比如，我可以把这个字母变成黄色，这个字母变成蓝色。
cues.en: So, I could turn this letter yellow, and this letter blue.

cues.zh: 我还可以把背景设为蓝色。
cues.en: And I could make the background blue.

cues.zh: 你看，这确实给原本黑白的显示增添了一些色彩。
cues.en: So, you can see how this certainly adds some color to an otherwise black and white display.

cues.zh: 每个颜色单元只需要 1 字节内存来定义前景色和背景色。
cues.en: And each color cell only requires 1 byte of memory to define the foreground and background colors.

cues.zh: 这意味着整个屏幕只用了 9 KB，而传统单色屏幕是 8 KB。
cues.en: That means the whole screen only used 9 kilobytes, instead of 8 kilobytes for a traditional monochrome screen.

cues.zh: 所以，这是个相当不错的取舍。
cues.en: So, that was a pretty good tradeoff.

cues.zh: 但问题也就从这里开始出现了。
cues.en: But, here's where you start to run into problems.

cues.zh: 举个例子，假设你想在这里画一条白线。
cues.en: Let's just say, for example, that you wanted to put a white line here.

cues.zh: 这其实做不到，因为每个单元只能有两种颜色。
cues.en: This would actually not be possible, because you can only have two colors per cell.

cues.zh: 所以，你能看到这种方法如何让电脑同时在屏幕上显示16种颜色，
cues.en: So, you can see how this method was able to give computers 16 colors on screen at the same time,

cues.zh: 只是你没法总是把颜色精确地放在你想要的位置。
cues.en: you just couldn't always put the colors exactly where you wanted them to go.

cues.zh: 你可以想象，这让艺术创作变得相当有挑战性。
cues.en: And you could imagine that this made artwork pretty challenging.

cues.zh: 尽管如此，看看这幅在Commodore 64上完成的作品。
cues.en: Nevertheless, take a look at this piece of artwork done on the Commodore 64.

cues.zh: 它看起来非常色彩丰富。
cues.en: It looks very colorful.

cues.zh: 而且，对外行人来说，他们甚至可能意识不到这台电脑的颜色限制。
cues.en: And, to the layman, they may not even be aware of the color limitations of the computer.

cues.zh: 但是，让我们放大这幅作品，
cues.en: But, let's zoom into this piece of art,

cues.zh: 再仔细看看。
cues.en: and look at it a little bit closer.

cues.zh: 如果我叠加一些假想的线条来显示颜色单元格的位置，
cues.en: If I overlay some imaginary lines to show you where the color cells are,

cues.zh: 你就能看到，实际上每个单元格里从来不超过2种颜色。
cues.en: you'll be able to see that, in fact, there are never more than 2 colors per cell.

cues.zh: 但是，艺术家非常努力地让他的作品与单元格的边缘对齐，
cues.en: But, the artist has worked very hard to make his work line up with the edges of the cells

cues.zh: 以至于看起来天衣无缝。
cues.en: to the point that it appears seamless.

cues.zh: 了解这一点后，你应该会对这些人所做的工作多几分敬意。
cues.en: Knowing this should cause you to give these guys a little bit more respect for the work they do.

cues.zh: 如果你是 NES 玩家，请记住几乎每款游戏都得处理这同一个问题。
cues.en: And, if you were a player of the Nintendo Entertainment System, then keep in mind just about every game had to deal with this exact same issue.

cues.zh: 色块的运作方式和 Commodore 64 略有不同，但基本上是同样的头疼事。
cues.en: The color cells worked a little bit different than the Commodore 64, but it's basically the same headache.

cues.zh: 所以工程师们知道这些颜色限制可能是个问题，
cues.en: So the engineers knew that these color limitations might be a problem,

cues.zh: 于是他们给软件设计师提供了另一个可用的选项。
cues.en: so they gave the software designers another option they could use.

cues.zh: 让我们回到双色示例。
cues.en: Let's go back to our 2-color example.

cues.zh: C64 有一个模式叫“多色模式”。
cues.en: The C64 had a mode called "multi-color mode".

cues.zh: 它的做法就是把像素宽度直接翻倍，
cues.en: Now, what it did was literally made the pixels twice as wide,

cues.zh: 这使屏幕分辨率减半。
cues.en: which cut the screen resolution in half.

cues.zh: 小号文字这样看起来非常糟糕。
cues.en: Small text looks really bad like this.

cues.zh: 但机器会为你的牺牲给予回报。你用一些分辨率换来了色彩。
cues.en: But the machine rewards you for your sacrifice. You have traded in some resolution for some color.

cues.zh: 但它仍然只占用9千字节的内存，就像另一个系统一样。
cues.en: But, it still only consumes 9 kilobytes of RAM, just like the other system.

cues.zh: 现在，每个色彩单元最多可显示4种颜色。
cues.en: Now, each color cell will allow you up to 4 colors.

cues.zh: 所以，现在你可以做这样的事情。
cues.en: So, now, you could do something like this.

cues.zh: 这是一个用多色模式创作的艺术作品示例。
cues.en: And here's an example of a piece of art done in multi-color mode.

cues.zh: 我再次放大展示细节，你可以看到这幅画中颜色是如何运用的。
cues.en: And again, I'll zoom in and show you the fine detail, and you can see how the colors were used in this picture.

cues.zh: 在单个单元中，你仍然不会看到超过4种颜色。
cues.en: You will still never see more than 4 colors used in a single cell.

cues.zh: Commodore 64上的大多数游戏实际上都使用了这种模式，因为色彩往往比高分辨率更重要。
cues.en: Most games for the Commodore 64 actually used this mode, since color was often more important than high resolution.

cues.zh: 工程师们还给了我们另一个工具，叫做硬件精灵生成器。现在让我展示它是如何工作的。
cues.en: And then there was one other tool the engineers gave us. It's called a hardware sprite generator. Now let me show you how this works.

cues.zh: 我要在方格纸上画一个精灵图。
cues.en: I'm going to create a sprite on graph paper.

cues.zh: 这其实是我在 1980 年代初学会的做法。
cues.en: This is actually how I learned to do this back in the early 1980s.

cues.zh: 接下来，我们得把它转成二进制数据。
cues.en: Next, we have to convert this to binary data.

cues.zh: 那么，我来演示一下怎么拆解。
cues.en: So, let me show you how to break this down.

cues.zh: 每个像素对应一个 0 或 1。
cues.en: Every pixel corresponds to a 0 or a 1.

cues.zh: 现在我把它分成三段，每段 8 个像素。
cues.en: Now I've divided this up into three sections of 8 pixels each.

cues.zh: 先看前 8 个像素。
cues.en: So, let's take the first 8 pixels.

cues.zh: 这里什么都没有，所以这一段写 0。
cues.en: There's nothing here, so we'll write in a 0 for this section.

cues.zh: 好，下一段确实有像素，为简单起见我用计算器把二进制转成十进制。
cues.en: Ok, the next section does have some pixels, and for simplicity I'll use a calculator to convert from binary to decimal.
So, we get 124.

cues.zh: 最后一段也是 0。
cues.en: And the last section will also be a 0.

cues.zh: 好，现在就这样一路填完整张纸。
cues.en: Okay, so now to finish all the way down the paper.

cues.zh: 好，接下来我把这些数字输入计算机内存。
cues.en: Ok, next I entered these numbers into the computer's memory.

cues.zh: 然后，我就能这样把精灵图显示出来。
cues.en: And, I can turn the sprite on like this.

cues.zh: 注意，我无法在精灵图上打字，也无法用键盘擦除它。
cues.en: Notice that I cannot type over the sprite, nor can I erase it using the keyboard.

cues.zh: 即使我改变文字的颜色，也无济于事。
cues.en: Even if I change the color of the text, it doesn't matter.

cues.zh: 精灵图独立于屏幕的其他部分，
cues.en: The sprite is independent from the rest of the screen,

cues.zh: 它甚至不关心颜色单元。
cues.en: and it doesn't even care about the color cells.

cues.zh: 我可以修改另一个寄存器，改变精灵图的颜色。
cues.en: I can modify a different register and change the color of the sprite.

cues.zh: 我可以修改另一个寄存器，把精灵图移到屏幕上的其他位置。
cues.en: I can change a different register, and move the sprite somewhere else on the screen.

cues.zh: 即使是清屏命令也无法清除它。
cues.en: Even a clear screen command won't get rid of it.

cues.zh: 精灵图在游戏中被大量使用。
cues.en: Sprites were heavily used in gaming.

cues.zh: 不同的系统有不同数量的精灵图。
cues.en: Different systems had different numbers of sprites.

cues.zh: Commodore 64 有 8 个不同的精灵图。
cues.en: The Commodore 64 had 8 different sprites.

cues.zh: 嗯，Nintendo 有 64 个精灵图，
cues.en: Um, the Nintendo had 64 sprites,

cues.zh: 但是，这些精灵图非常小，意味着你通常需要多用很多个才能达到同样的目的。
cues.en: but, the sprites were very small, meaning you would usually need to use a lot more of them to accomplish the same goal.

cues.zh: 所以，这里的 Mario 实际上是由几个不同的精灵组成的，
cues.en: So, Mario here was actually made up of several different sprites,

cues.zh: 但他们把它们很好地组合在一起，所以看起来、动起来就像一个整体。
cues.en: but they just do a good job of keeping them all together so it looks and behaves like one.

cues.zh: 好了，第一部分就到这里。请继续关注第二部分，我会给你们展示 Apple II 图形以及一些早期由 CPU 驱动的图形模式是如何工作的。
cues.en: All right, so this concludes part one. Stick around for part two, where I'm going to show you how Apple II graphics and some of the early CPU-driven graphics modes worked.
